d: causative action by which someone builds or repairs a wall, often made of natural stones; ≈ such a wall is sometimes used to denote integrity, which can be negatively affected by sin
causative action by which someone blocks the entrance, passage, or access (in)to a building, construction, or area ◄ with a door
literally: to put a seal on an object; hence: = causative action by which an opening or entrance is closed so that nothing can enter or leave, ◄ as if kept from being opened with a seal
action or process by which the functioning of something is prevented or stopped
action by which humans secure a door or a lid so that it cannot be opened, ► usually to restrict access to a room or a space
causative action by which humans or deities close the entrance to a space with the help of a {L:door<SDBH:דֶּלֶת>}
literally: to cover; hence: = action by which deities close an opening with an object to prevent a substance from coming out
process by which a physical opening is closed
action by which humans clog or block a natural flow of water
causative action by which humans attach one or more objects to another object that contains an opening ► in order to block entry and/or exit
causative action by which humans build a fence around a certain place, ► which provides security from danger from outside, but also restricts movement for those within
state in which human eyes are closed ► as a result of which they are unable to see, ≈ with the connotation of being unwilling to face reality
